title: 10-Year TIPS auction (NEW ISSUE) — the only place a TIPS size change has ever expressed, and the first real-yield print of 2027
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-08 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) by the treasury-10y-tips-2026-11-19 initial research, text layer decompressed stream-by-stream and re-tokenised into 213 (security, announce, auction, settle) rows. Row reads verbatim `10-Year TIPS T / Announcement Thursday, January 14, 2027 / Auction Thursday, January 21, 2027 / Settlement Friday, January 29, 2027`. Treasury's trailing `T` marks TIPS and the ABSENCE of an `R` is what makes this a NEW ISSUE rather than a reopening — the same marker convention the 5-Year TIPS 2026-10-22 entry reads. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. The CUSIP does not exist yet and is not guessed. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: DISCOVERED during the treasury-10y-tips-2026-11-19 never-assessed initial research (2026-09-08). PROPOSED DESPITE SITTING 63 DAYS PAST ITS PROPOSER, because it is that event's structural terminus and it dates a claim the calendar was carrying undated. The treasury-coupon-announcement-2026-11-12 ledger's central finding is an asymmetry — a TIPS size change has NEVER expressed at a reopening; every step in the 10-Year series (17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21) landed on a January or July NEW ISSUE — from which it concluded that an increase announced at the 2026-11-04 refunding 'would structurally surface at the January 2027 new issue, not here.' This row is that January 2027 new issue, with a Treasury-primary announcement date (2027-01-14) and auction date attached, so the claim becomes scoreable instead of directional. IT ALSO CLOSES 91282CRE3's LIFE: the absence of an `R` here means the 2026-11-19 auction is the last time that CUSIP is ever sold, which is what makes 2026-11-19 the final 10-Year real-yield primary print of 2026. SIZE EXPECTATION, for whoever researches it: the new-issue ratchet has been FLAT at $21B for three consecutive new issues (2025-07-24, 2026-01-22, 2026-07-23) after rising every year 2019-2025 (13 -> 14 -> 15 -> 16 -> 17 -> 18 -> 19 -> 20 -> 21), so $21B is the base case and any change to it is the event's whole information content — fiscaldata auctions_query, `inflation_index_security: Yes`, back to 2019-01-01, pulled 2026-09-08. The 63-day gap from 2026-11-19 is the ORDINARY inter-auction interval, not an unusual one: 2026's six 10-Year TIPS auctions run 56/63/63/56/63 days apart, so this is tied-longest and nothing more — recorded because the opposite claim was tempting and is false. Proposed as an estimate; symbols: [] and no house playbook is rates-keyed, so nothing here licenses an entry.
